name: Coffee
description: Roasted bean brew, espresso to qahwa.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates coffee mildly and marks no mechanism on it: the concern is that caffeine stimulates nerves and bowel, which can activate mast cells. It is not a DAO blocker.
histamine.why: SIGHI calls caffeine possibly mast-cell activating but stops short of assigning the liberator letter. Taseer assigns it, and scores a point higher to match.

nutrition.highlight: caffeine, and more of it in a light roast

stimulant.note: Caffeine and essentially nothing to soften it, which is why coffee comes on fast and leaves fast.

effects.note: Caffeinated coffee measurably speeds up colon movement within minutes of drinking it — one study clocked it at roughly 60% stronger than the same amount of water, with decaf producing a smaller version of the same effect, which points to more than caffeine alone at work. Only around three in ten people in that study actually felt the urge, though, so this is a more unevenly-felt effect than most on this list. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.

Large cohort studies find coffee drinkers develop cirrhosis and advanced liver fibrosis less often, with a clear dose-response — each extra two cups a day tracks with roughly half the pooled cirrhosis risk across studies spanning several hundred thousand people, holding up whether the underlying cause is alcohol or viral hepatitis. This is observational evidence rather than a randomised trial, and the same benefit shows up with decaf, pointing to compounds like chlorogenic acid working alongside caffeine rather than caffeine driving it alone. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
